newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH INDMIN DETAILS IMPORT DEPOSITS PROCEDURE.
newsitem.headline: CZECH INDMIN DETAILS IMPORT DEPOSITS PROCEDURE.

text.p: Five Czech commercial banks have been chosen to collect import deposits which will be required as of Monday, Industry and Trade Minister Vladimir Dlouhy said on Thursday.
Dlouhy told reporters these would be the country's largest banks, Komercni Banka a.s., Ceska Sporitelna a.s. , IPB a.s., Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka a.s., and Union Banka a.s. .
The state holds large stakes in all the banks except for Union Banka.
The cabinet unveiled a package of measures on Wednesday aimed at revitalising economic growth and eliminating budget and current account deficits.
Under the scheme, importers will be required to deposit 20 percent of the value of imported goods on an interest-free account for 180 days.
Dlouhy said that the commercial banks would channel the money from their branches to state-held development bank Konsolidacni Banka s.p.u..
"The chosen commercial banks will receive 0.5 percent of the sum as a reimbursement," Dlouhy said.
He estimated the money on import deposits would accumulate to some 24 billion crowns over the first six months.
Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus said on Thursday that he believed the import restriction along with other measures would have a marginal effect on inflation.
"We expect that it will contribute to a reversal in the trend of an increasing deficit of the trade balance, (this year)," Klaus told a news conference.

Other measures taken by the cabinet include 25.5 billion in budget cuts, limiting 1997 wage growth in the public sector to 7.3 percent, setting up an independent capital market oversight body, promoting exports, and fighting more intensively against economic crime.

The package of new policies, which has been welcomed by the markets and analysts, also calls for speeding up privatisation of state-held companies, relaxation of monetary policy, and separation of the investment and commercial arms of banks.
